newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina announces new quality wheat grade.
newsitem.headline: Argentina announces new quality wheat grade.

text.p: Argentina's Agricultural Secretary Felipe Sola announced Wednesday the creation of a new, higher quality grade of Argentine wheat.
Sola told a news conference that the creation of the new grade, to be marketed as "plata", which means "silver" in Spanish, should help Argentine producers maximize prices.
"There is world demand for Argentine wheat, but this demand is more selective all the time," he said.
Sola said the new grade will be used as of the coming 1997/98 season.

Plata wheat will have a maximum 13 percent humidity, a minimum hectolictric weight of 81 kg, and a 13-percent minimum protein level. It will have a minimum wet gluten level of 32 percent, a minimum falling number of 350 and a maximum 1.7 percent ash content.

Sola also announced a new "Argentine soft white wheat" grade. Although this sort of wheat -- aimed at biscuit and cracker makers -- is not currently produced in Argentina, Sola said the government hoped the creation of the new grade would encourage its production.
The new wheat will be white to prevent its being mixed with hard wheats.
Argentine soft white wheat will have a minimum protein level of less than 10 percent.
